scope: Proposition 2.2 of the manuscript “A Counterexample to the Group-Ring Determinant Conjecture” (preprints/A-Counterexample-to-the-Group-Ring-Determinant-Conjecture-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 197 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3524b6f2390f17d5), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let X, Y ∈ Md(F2[H2]), d ≥ 1, satisfy XY = Id ̸= Y X. In the group GD = ( ⨁︁ h∈H2 C3) ⋊ H2, where H2 acts by left translation on coordinate labels, there is an orthogonal projection P ∈ Md+1(Z[1/3][GD]) and a finite set S ⊆ H2 \ {1} such that τd+1(P) = d + θ, θ = 1 3 (︃ 2 3 )︃|S| > 0, P̄ = uv, where u has size (d + 1) × d and v has size d × (d + 1) over F2[GD]. The integer D = 31+|S| clears all coefficients of P.
